A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SimbaV2 research and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices A–K. Cross-checking local renderers resolved initial display gaps, enabling a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original SimbaV2 evaluations on 57 online-control tasks, nine offline D4RL settings, scaling experiments, training-dynamics analyses, and architectural ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains those original empirical results and adds critic-depth scaling and DDPG-based architectural comparisons.

M1.justification: Equation (17) changes the specified reward-scaling return update from G_t = (1−γ)G_{t−1}+r_t to G_t = γG_{t−1}+r_t. This changes the documented return statistics, but the PDFs do not establish an implementation change or rerun. The remaining architecture, losses, normalization components, and updates are retained.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 57 online tasks across MuJoCo, DMC, MyoSuite, and HumanoidBench, plus nine offline D4RL settings. The added depth and DDPG experiments reuse DMC-Hard and HBench-Hard without changing task requirements or environments.

E2.justification: v2 adds REDQ and DroQ to the MuJoCo comparisons in Tables 1 and 16 and an MLP control to the new DDPG study. It removes SR-SAC from the DMC-Hard comparison in Table 18 and CQN-AS from HumanoidBench Table 20. Most comparator membership remains unchanged.

E3.justification: v2 adds a critic-depth sweep over L = 1, 2, 4, 8, spanning 2.2M–17.8M parameters, and evaluates three architectures using DDPG. The added REDQ/DroQ comparisons use UTD 20. Existing benchmark metrics, one-million-step budgets, and width/UTD scaling protocols are retained.

E4.justification: Two distinct analyses substantially extend validation: Figure 6 tests sensitivity to critic depth, while Appendix H.2 tests whether architectural benefits extend beyond SAC to DDPG. These address questions absent from v1's width/UTD scaling, training-dynamics, and component-ablation studies, which remain present.

E5.justification: SAC's MuJoCo aggregate confidence intervals lose the dagger indicating approximation from task averages in Tables 1 and 16, changing the documented uncertainty basis. The general confidence-interval and Welch-test procedures remain unchanged, and the SAC results still report ten seeds rather than an increased run count.

E6.justification: New depth curves show SimbaV2 benefiting from deeper critics, and new DDPG curves show competitive performance with Simba on DMC-Hard and stronger performance on HBench-Hard. Tables 1 and 16 add REDQ/DroQ results and replace SAC's MuJoCo mean of 0.934 with 1.092 using a different source, so this is not an established same-setting gain. Tables 18 and 20 remove baseline results. Table 1 also changes SimbaV2's HBench uncertainty from ±0.071 to ±0.064; its overall means of 0.892 and 0.911 remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Equation (17) corrects the mathematical definition of the running discounted return by replacing the coefficient 1−γ with γ. Appendix A's Riemannian-retraction and scaler-initialization derivations and Appendix G's metric definitions are unchanged; no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central claims of stabilizing norms, scaling model size and compute without periodic resets, and strong performance across 57 online tasks. Separating feature and weight normalization into distinct contribution bullets does not introduce a new core contribution.

C2.justification: v2 interprets depth saturation around L = 4 on DMC-Hard as likely reflecting task complexity and attributes deeper-network stability to regularization. Appendix H.2 interprets the DDPG findings as evidence of effectiveness beyond SAC. The introduction also expands explanations linking norm growth to optimization and plasticity problems.

D1.justification: Appendix E replaces the MuJoCo SAC source with results obtained from the Bhatt et al. authors and newly specifies SAC and Simba UTD settings. It documents REDQ/DroQ provenance and settings, while Appendix H.2 briefly specifies the linear/ReLU MLP control. Existing JAX listings and default hyperparameter tables are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations and discussion concerning mixture-of-experts scaling, value classification, and norm/plasticity mechanisms, including Obando-Ceron, Willi, Farebrother, Kumar, Hussing, and Ma. It removes the Henderson/Eimer tuning-focused discussion. These refine positioning while preserving the relationship to Simba and prior hyperspherical architectures.

P1.justification: The introduction is rewritten around three norm-instability mechanisms, Empirical Analysis is split into Optimization Analysis and Scaling Analysis, and Appendix H gains subsections. A generic Impact Statement, expanded acknowledgments, and conference publication text are added. Most method explanations and existing appendices retain their structure and wording.

P2.justification: v2 adds depth and DDPG plots, changes Figure 5's horizontal axis from parameter counts to critic hidden dimensions, and modifies comparator rows or columns in Tables 1, 16, 18, and 20. Existing displays are largely retained and reflowed. Figure 1's revised caption introduces a BRO UTD inconsistency: 8 in the caption versus 10 in the plotted point.

improvement.justification: The depth sweep and DDPG study strengthen evidence for scalability and effectiveness beyond SAC, while correcting Equation (17) improves the method specification. These gains are limited by sparse DDPG implementation details and reporting inconsistencies: Figure 1 mislabels BRO's UTD, and Table 1 retains SAC's overall score of 0.554 after replacing its MuJoCo scores. The additional validation nevertheless supports a modest net quality improvement.
